deep_analysis.executive_intro:
Across the full FTSE screen, actionable bullish signals are a minority: 16 Strong Buys and 46 Buys versus 143 Holds and 43 Avoids, so the run reads as selective rather than broad risk-on. The five highest-ranked names are all labelled Strong Buy with full metric coverage (20/20) and persistent signals (15 weeks, stable), but several carry overlay downgrades to Buy on FCF basis, dividend sustainability, or interim quality. Sector clustering is pronounced at the top: three of five leaders are Industrials (FirstGroup, ME Group, Morgan Sindall), with Communication Services (ITV) and Healthcare (Hikma) rounding out the list. A central caution is data integrity: multiple top names show FCF basis mismatches (filing vs screen TTM vs company-adjusted), unverified screen TTM figures, and statutory vs management dividend-coverage divergence—the screen passes yield-dependent models only after those overlays, so headline Strong Buy labels understate accounting noise.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models pass with composite score 89% and all five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk); highlights include P/E 8.5, P/B 1.3, yield 4.2%, ROE 16.7%, screen D/E 19%, Lynch PEG 0.53 on 16% earnings growth, Piotroski F-Score 8/9, and passes on Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Earnings Quality, and Composite Value. Failures include Financial Health (weak liquidity; current ratio 0.73), Economic Moat, and Graham Defensive; FCF policy uses company-adjusted £113.5M versus filing £362.6M and screen TTM £302.8M (unverified), with adjusted_signal Buy after FCF basis overlay. Industrials concentration: two other top-five names share the same sector peer set. **Verdict: accumulate** — valuation and quality screens are unusually aligned, but size only after reconciling which FCF definition supports the dividend (net coverage ~2.9× on company-adjusted FCF).

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models pass (composite 81%, sector-relative 88%) with P/E 8.2, P/B 2.3, yield 6.8%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%; standout passes include Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Buffett Quality, Magic Formula, and Financial Health, while Lynch PEG fails (0.4% model growth, PEG 22.54), Piotroski 6/9, and Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion). Interim dividend cut is flagged; statutory OCF−CapEx dividend cover is 0.84× versus management basis 1.68×; statutory EPS growth 4.5% vs filing core 0.4% (>300 bps divergence); adjusted_signal Buy after interim-quality and FCF overlays. Third Industrials name among top picks increases sector correlation. **Verdict: watchlist** — headline cheapness and moat scores conflict with dividend cut, thin real growth, and sub-1× statutory FCF dividend cover.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models pass (composite 79%) with P/E 11.7, P/B 1.5, yield 7.2%, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%, 23% earnings growth, Lynch PEG 0.51, and passes on High Dividend Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health; Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, and Piotroski F-Score 3/9 fail (broad deterioration flags on ROA, leverage, margins, and cash conversion). Timing is “accumulate” (score 0.75), price ~10.5% below 200-day MA; dividend-sustainability overlay applied (statutory cover 1.0×, management 1.53×); FCF filing £148M vs company-adj £187M vs unverified screen TTM £211.9M; adjusted_signal Buy. **Verdict: accumulate** — timing and income/value screens align, but treat the 7.2% yield as provisional until Piotroski and statutory FCF cover are validated in filings.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — Twelve of 22 models pass (composite 78%, sector-relative 86%) with P/E 11.8, P/B 1.8, yield 4.2%, ROE 15.4%, D/E 77%, growth 1.7%; passes include Graham Enterprising, Buffett Quality, Quality Value, Financial Health, and Composite Value; FCF Yield fails (3.8% vs 5% hurdle), Lynch PEG fails, Piotroski 6/9, and Earnings Quality fails on weak free-cash conversion. FCF filing $119M vs unverified screen TTM $14.4M; statutory FCF dividend cover 0.64× vs management 1.31×; heavy capex (£317M) vs OCF £436M in cashflow_metrics. **Verdict: watchlist** — healthcare generic/value case is plausible on P/E and balance sheet, but cash conversion and sub-5% FCF yield undermine the full “cheap cash” story.

**MGNS.L (Morgan Sindall Group plc)** — Strongest model count in the top five at 16/22 (composite 81%) with P/E 10.5, P/B 2.4, yield 4.1%, ROE 26.1%, D/E 18%, 19.6% earnings growth, Lynch PEG 0.54, Piotroski 8/9, FCF yield 9.0%, and clean passes on Earnings Quality, Financial Health, FCF Yield, and Piotroski; Economic Moat fails on ROA and margins. FCF basis mismatch filing £170.7M vs unverified screen TTM £141.5M; FCF dividend coverage net ~2.6×; adjusted_signal Buy after FCF overlay only. Fourth Industrials exposure alongside FGP and MEGP. **Verdict: accumulate** — broadest quantitative confirmation in the peer industrial cluster with relatively cleaner earnings quality and FCF versus FGP/MEGP.

- FGP.L: Public transport/concession and contract renewal risk, fuel and wage inflation, and UK policy on bus/rail funding are not in the screen; open question whether lease-adjusted net debt (£137.7m filing) fully captures long-term transport obligations.
- FGP.L: Governance and capital allocation around FCF definition (company-adjusted £113.5M vs filing-aligned £362.6M) — open question on what management treats as recurring cash.
- MEGP.L: Photo-booth / travel-adjacent revenue cyclicality and airport/traffic volumes not modelled; interim dividend cut may signal structural not temporary payout pressure — open question on full-year dividend policy.
- MEGP.L: Statutory vs core EPS growth divergence (>300 bps) — open question on one-offs distorting “value” P/E 8.2.
- ITV.L: Structural decline in linear TV, advertising cyclicality, and regulatory/plurality obligations for UK broadcasters not captured; Piotroski 3/9 suggests operational stress the value screen may lag.
- ITV.L: High yield (7.2%) with dividend-sustainability overlay — open question on studio strategy, debt refi, and whether earnings growth (23%) is durable vs content spend cycles.
- HIK.L: US FDA/import regulation, patent cliffs, and pricing pressure in generics/injectables not in quantitative moat failure set beyond ROE/ROA thresholds.
- HIK.L: USD reporting vs GBP listing — FX and dividend repatriation not screened; statutory FCF cover 0.64× raises open question on dividend safety if capex stays elevated.
- MGNS.L: UK construction and public-sector project cyclicality, margin risk on fixed-price contracts, and pension deficit (if any) not in JSON — open question on backlog quality through a downturn.
- MGNS.L: Economic Moat fail (thin margins vs screen thresholds) — open question on competitive bidding vs ROE 26.1% sustainability.

question_outcomes.question: Governance and capital allocation around FCF definition (company-adjusted £113.5M vs filing-aligned £362.6M) — open question on what management treats as recurring cash.
question_outcomes.evidence: Management’s published definition (FY 2025 results presentation, `filings/bodies/ir_5ba5b17047f87036.txt`) states that “Free cash flow” is the movement in adjusted net debt excluding disposal proceeds and cash outflows for dividends, share buybacks, and acquisitions; the appendix reconciles statutory FCF £385.9m to company-adjusted £113.5m for FY 2025 via ring-fenced TOC cash, IFRS 16, and other columns. FY 2026 results RNS (`filings/bodies/3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`) applies the same construct at £73.8m (prior year £113.5m) with a divisional bridge. The newly ingested Companies House group annual report extract (`filings/bodies/ch_SC157176_MzUzNzM4MjMyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt`, filed August 2026) repeats the strategic-report highlight of £73.8m free cash flow before acquisitions and returns and c.£400m free cash generation anticipated over three years, consistent with the June 2026 RNS but without a clean statutory-to-adjusted table (OCR-only highlights). The 1 July 2026 annual report NSM notice (`filings/bodies/d45784fca483323c.txt`) points to full PDF statements on the company site; that PDF body is not yet in `filings/bodies/`.

Capital allocation narrative ties surplus cash to multi-year generation (c.£400m over three years in RNS; CH annual highlights echo this) and bus capex normalisation toward c.£80–100m from FY 2028 after elevated electrification spend. The screen’s company-adjusted £113.5m and ~2.9× dividend coverage align with **FY 2025** adjusted FCF, not FY 2026 £73.8m (~1.9× gross dividend cash cover on £38.9m paid). documents.name: FirstGroup plc
documents.executive_summary: FirstGroup is a UK-focused bus and rail operator emerging from a multi-year portfolio reset, with adjusted revenue of £1,715.7m in FY 2026 (52 weeks to 28 March 2026) and a capital-return story anchored on buybacks and a progressive dividend. The quantitative screen rates the stock a strong buy (15/22 models, composite ~89%), supported by low multiples (P/E ~8.5, yield ~4.2%), solid adjusted earnings growth, and filing-adjusted net debt of £137.7m. The central debate is whether open-access rail, London Overground, and bus diversification can offset DfT TOC renationalisation, weak regional bus volumes, and heavy electrification capex—and which free-cash-flow definition fairly supports the yield screens. FCF metrics diverge materially (£73.8m company “free cash flow before acquisitions and returns” in FY 2026 results versus £362.6m statutory OCF less capex in the same release; screen company-adjusted FCF £113.5m), so valuation comfort rests on management-adjusted earnings and balance-sheet leverage policy, not a single FCF line.
documents.investment_thesis: The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a business that now passes cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families (5/5), with Piotroski F-Score 8/9 and persistent signal (~15 weeks). FirstGroup combines enterprising-style valuation (low P/E, earnings yield, Lynch PEG ~0.53 on ~16% earnings growth) with improving operational narrative: adjusted EPS rose from 19.4p (FY 2025) to 20.3p (FY 2026), dividend per share to 7.2p, and the board launched a further £100m buyback while guiding ~£400m free cash generation over three years. Quality is not “wide moat” by screen (Economic Moat fails on ROE/margins), but post-North America divestiture the group is a cleaner UK transport compounder—First Bus London, coach bolt-ons, open access (Lumo/Hull Trains), and contract wins (London Overground preferred operator, December 2025 RNS)—with management explicitly targeting adjusted net debt below 2.0x Rail adjusted EBITDA. For a value investor, the hook is statistically cheap equity on adjusted earnings, net debt near £138m on a pre-IFRS-16 basis, and management returning surplus cash; the screen’s leverage override (Yahoo D/E ~161% vs filing-adjusted net debt) is directionally correct because lease gross-up obscures economic leverage.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates a large, geographically diversified estate of photobooths and fast-growing unattended laundry machines, with FY2025 record profit before tax of £78.2m on revenue of £315.4m (RNS annual results, 23 March 2026). The quantitative screen rates the stock a strong buy on cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk buckets (15/22 models; composite ~81%; P/E ~8.2, yield ~6.8%, ROE ~28%, debt/equity ~28%), but overlays flag interim dividend reduction, weak statutory free-cash-flow dividend cover and earnings-growth definition gaps. The valuation hook is a cash-generative, asset-heavy vending franchise trading at a low multiple while laundry mix rises; the key debate is whether photobooth/regulatory and consumer cyclicality (France, Germany) plus higher capex and accounting/audit noise justify the discount—or signal structural pressure on earnings and distributions.
documents.investment_thesis: For a value investor, MEGP combines enterprising Graham-style metrics (low P/E, high yield, moderate leverage, positive operating cash flow) with unusually strong reported returns on equity and a rare “economic moat” pass among UK industrial peers in the screen snapshot. Primary filings support a quality narrative: FY2025 cash generated from operations of £115.5m, net cash of £26.5m (excluding lease liabilities), and laundry revenue up 17.3% to £112.4m while the estate expanded (7,607 Wash.ME units). The screen’s quality and dividend families align with management’s capital-return posture (FY2025 total dividend 8.64p, +9.5%; £18m buyback launched post-results), but the same filing set shows growth is increasingly capex-led (FY2025 capex £65.6m) and photobooth revenue fell 4.0% on German ID rules and supply issues. H1 FY2026 interim results (13 July 2026) show laundry still accelerating (Wash.ME revenue +16.3%) yet group PBT down 3.8% to £32.7m and full-year PBT guidance cut to £69m–£74m—so the strong-buy signal rests on trailing full-year economics and multiples more than on near-term earnings momentum. Failed screen models (Lynch PEG on ~0.4% adjusted EPS growth, Piotroski 6/9, earnings quality) are consistent with that tension: cheap on headline numbers, less compelling on forward growth and cash conversion consistency.

documents.name: ITV plc
documents.executive_summary: ITV plc screens as a strong buy on cheapness, dividend yield, and broad value-model pass rates, against a business in the middle of a defining strategic shift: the agreed sale of Media & Entertainment (M&E) to Sky for up to £1.6bn, with a planned ~£950m cash return to shareholders and a post-completion pure-play ITV Studios listing. The valuation hook is a low headline multiple and a ~7% dividend yield on a name that has rebuilt digital momentum (ITVX) while growing Studios exposure. The central debate is whether today’s screen metrics—built largely on the integrated group—still describe the residual equity story after regulatory clearance, separation costs, pension mitigation, and cyclical UK advertising. Filing-backed cash generation in FY2025 was materially below the prior year, and statutory free cash flow sits closer to one times dividend cover than management-adjusted measures imply.
documents.investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen (15/22 models passing, composite 79%, all five families: cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) flags ITV as unusually cheap for a FTSE communications name: P/E ~11.7, P/B ~1.5, dividend yield ~7.2%, debt/equity ~52%, with Lynch PEG ~0.51 on ~23% earnings growth in the screen inputs. That aligns with a classic value setup: market scepticism toward linear TV, plus event risk around the Sky transaction, has compressed the rating despite resilient adjusted profits and an explicit capital-return pathway.

Business quality is mixed relative to the screen. Filings show strategic execution under “More than TV”: FY2024 group adjusted EBITA rose 11% to £542m; FY2025 adjusted EBITA was resilient at £534m (down 1%) despite a 5% decline in total advertising revenue (TAR), with Studios external revenue +10% and digital revenue +10%. ITVX viewing and digital ad growth remain positive operational signals. However, the screen fails high-bar quality checks (Piotroski F-Score 3/9; Buffett/moat models on ROE and margins), and overlays already flag dividend sustainability and free-cash-flow definition divergence (statutory OCF−CapEx cover ~1.0× vs management “cash generated” ~1.53×). For a value investor, the strong-buy signal is best read as “mispriced integrated cash flows plus optional upside from monetisation,” not as proof of durable moat quality—especially as the listed entity is poised to become Studios-centric with regulatory and execution risk attached.

question_outcomes.question: Governance and capital allocation around FCF definition (company-adjusted £113.5M vs filing-aligned £362.6M) — open question on what management treats as recurring cash.
question_outcomes.evidence: Management’s published definition (FY 2025 results presentation, `filings/bodies/ir_5ba5b17047f87036.txt`) states that “Free cash flow” is the movement in adjusted net debt excluding disposal proceeds and cash outflows for dividends, share buybacks, and acquisitions; the appendix reconciles statutory FCF £385.9m to company-adjusted £113.5m for FY 2025 via ring-fenced TOC cash, IFRS 16, and other columns. FY 2026 results RNS (`filings/bodies/3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`) applies the same construct at £73.8m (prior year £113.5m) with a divisional bridge. The newly ingested Companies House group annual report extract (`filings/bodies/ch_SC157176_MzUzNzM4MjMyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt`, filed August 2026) repeats the strategic-report highlight of £73.8m free cash flow before acquisitions and returns and c.£400m free cash generation anticipated over three years, consistent with the June 2026 RNS but without a clean statutory-to-adjusted table (OCR-only highlights). The 1 July 2026 annual report NSM notice (`filings/bodies/d45784fca483323c.txt`) points to full PDF statements on the company site; that PDF body is not yet in `filings/bodies/`.

question_outcomes.question: Which free cash flow definition (filing £362.6M, screen TTM £302.8M unverified, or company-adj £113.5M) should anchor dividend and buyback capacity after lease and working-capital normalisation?
question_outcomes.evidence: For FY 2026, filing-aligned FCF remains operating cash flow £615.6m less capex £253.0m = £362.6m (RNS cash-flow table in `3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`; Yahoo `financials_annual.json` matches). That line is not what the board uses for returns: company-adjusted FCF is £73.8m (FY 2025: £113.5m), with cash dividends paid £38.9m and buybacks £50.4m in FY 2026—aggregate returns (~£89m per RNS highlights) above single-year adjusted FCF. Capital allocation narrative ties surplus cash to multi-year generation (c.£400m over three years in RNS; CH annual highlights echo this) and bus capex normalisation toward c.£80–100m from FY 2028 after elevated electrification spend. The screen’s company-adjusted £113.5m and ~2.9× dividend coverage align with **FY 2025** adjusted FCF, not FY 2026 £73.8m (~1.9× gross dividend cash cover on £38.9m paid). Screen TTM £302.8m stays unverified (no Yahoo quarterly cashflow). New CH interim body (`ch_SC157176_MzQ5MDA3NTQ5MmFkaXF6a2N4.txt`) is **parent-company** unaudited accounts only and does not add group FCF.

question_outcomes.question: (FirstGroup plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models pass with composite score 89% … **Verdict: accumulate** — valuation and quality screens unusually aligned, but size only after reconciling which FCF definition supports the dividend (net coverage ~2.9× on company-adjusted FCF).
question_outcomes.evidence: `screening_snapshot.json` still shows strong_buy (15/22, composite ~89%, FCF basis overlay, adjusted_signal buy) with company-adjusted FCF £113.5m in the action note. Follow-up filing work confirms FY 2026 company-adjusted FCF is **£73.8m**, so FCF-yield and dividend-sustainability overlays that rely on £113.5m overstate near-term cash headroom unless normalisation and the three-year cash guide are credited. Cheapness/quality passes (P/E ~8.5, Piotroski 8/9, Lynch PEG ~0.53) remain filing-supported; Financial Health fail (liquidity) unchanged. Accumulate stance holds, but sizing should use **latest-year** adjusted FCF (£73.8m) plus explicit forward guide, not stale £113.5m.
